correctness.rationale: For each unbounded-direction set S of a finite ray-graph, extended Hausdorff distance between direction classes is infinite. The source constructs H_t(A) as the radius ρ(t)=t/(1−t) neighborhood, under the metric d_t scaling excluded rays by (1−t)^{-2}, of g_t(A), where g_t shortens each ray coordinate x to max(0,x−t/(1−t)). It starts at A and preserves nonempty closed sets, the at-most-n component bound, and the set of unbounded rays: a finite thickening of a connected subset in a path-metric graph is connected, while finite shifts/neighborhoods preserve unbounded-ray membership. For t→1, tails in S are shifted to entire rays and all core edges are filled, whereas spill on excluded rays has original length at most ρ/w=t(1−t). The finite core and Hausdorff-local uniform tail thresholds prove joint continuity, so H_1(A)=Y_S defines a genuine contraction. The k=0 case yields a single contractible component; no claim in the Vietoris topology is needed.
residual_risks: Continuity requires finite ray count and Hausdorff-local uniform bounds; omitted infinite-ray/Vietoris cases are not covered.
Unindexed strengthening in graph hyperspace literature may duplicate the deformation.

The weighted metric is a nontrivial continuity mechanism to prevent excluded rays from proliferating.
